title: Validation Evidence
description:
What happened when one `command` check from a task's frozen validation plan was actually run (plan §6).

Evidence binds the observation to what it was an observation *of*: the exact candidate (`candidateRevision`) and the exact semantic input snapshot (`inputSnapshotDigest`). Both are load-bearing, and for the same reason an approval names both — a passing test attached only to a commit survives the contract changing underneath it, which is how a green gate comes to mean nothing. Staleness is derived by comparing these against current truth, never stored: a `stale` flag stops being true the moment the candidate moves and nobody goes back to update it (plan §17 Scenario 5).

A gate reads this file to decide whether work may proceed, so the record is sealed by `recordDigest` and the seal is checked on every read. But the seal covers the *whole* record, unlike handoff.schema.json and review-decision.schema.json, which digest a substance-only half so that recording the same statement twice is detectable. That split is deliberate there and deliberately absent here: a judgement made twice is suspicious, while an observation made twice is ordinary — rerunning the suite on the same candidate is what a careful Agent does, and the second run is a second fact rather than a duplicate of the first. Sealing everything, `seq` and `recordedAt` included, says "this record is as it was written" without also claiming "this observation is unique".

Only `command` checks produce evidence. A `review` check is answered from the review decision itself, which is already a first-class artifact; recording a second copy of a judgement here would create two places that could disagree about what the reviewer said.

evidenceId.description: Assigned by the ledger as evidence:<check-id>-<seq>. The sequence number is part of the id because reruns are expected: the same check against the same candidate can be observed more than once, and each observation needs its own name.

seq.description: Position in this session's evidence order, assigned under the session lock. Evidence for different tasks and checks interleaves, so this is the only total ordering available.

checkId.description: Which check in the task's frozen plan this is evidence for. Resolved against that plan when recorded, so evidence cannot be filed for a check the task never declared.

candidateRevision.description: Exactly what was tested. Any revision scheme, not only git, for the same reason review decisions allow it: plan §13 anticipates naming a work-product digest instead of a commit so that a rebase changing no substance does not discard the result.

inputSnapshotDigest.description: The task's input snapshot at the time of the run. Copied from the frozen task rather than asserted by the runner, so it cannot describe a snapshot the check was not actually run against.

resultDigest.description: sha256 over the whole captured output, so a recorded result cannot be quietly restated later. Note what this is not: two passing runs of the same suite will not share a digest, because real output carries timings and counts. It identifies an observation; it does not compare them.

exitCode.description: The process exit status, or null when there was none — the check errored before exiting, or was killed. Kept alongside `status` because `failed` says the candidate is wrong while the exit code often says how.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock milliseconds. Not a digested part of the result: the same check on the same candidate takes a different time every run, and treating that as substance would make every rerun look like a different observation.

outputExcerpt.description: The tail of the captured output, up to 2000 characters. The tail rather than the head because a failing run puts the reason at the end and the head is setup noise. Empty is legitimate — a quiet command that exits 0 says everything by exiting 0.

outputTruncated.description: Whether output was dropped from the excerpt. Recorded explicitly so a reader can tell a short run from a truncated one; the digest still covers the full output either way.

note.description: Why an `errored` check could not tell us anything — a missing binary, a timeout, a signal. Present only when the runner has something to say that the exit code cannot.

recordDigest.description: sha256 over every other field of this record, checked on every read. A gate consults evidence to decide whether work may proceed, so a `status` that could be edited from `failed` to `passed` on disk would be a pass anyone could manufacture — the same reason review decisions are sealed. Verified on read rather than offered as a separate `verify` command, because a check nobody runs is not a check.
